<a id="SEC-001"></a>
# SLCR CLI

The requirements of `slcr`, the reference command-line implementation of SLCR specifications, written as an SLCR specification and checked by `slcr check`.

<a id="SEC-003"></a>
## 1. Commands

The subcommands `slcr` offers. Each is a requirement whose behaviors refine it, so a subcommand is satisfied exactly when all of its behaviors are. Unless a requirement says otherwise, a subcommand that succeeds exits with status 0, one that fails exits with status 1 and explains why on stderr, and a usage error, such as an unknown argument or a missing one, exits with status 2 and prints the subcommand's usage.

<a id="REQ-001"></a>
### 1.1 version

`slcr` MUST have a `version` subcommand that prints the version of the running CLI.

*Rationale:* Users and bug reports need to know which release of `slcr` produced an output.

All of the following must hold:

- [Prints the package version](#REQ-002)
- [version usage](#REQ-003)

<a id="REQ-002"></a>
#### 1.1.1 Prints the package version

`slcr version` MUST write `v`, the package version from `Cargo.toml`, and a newline to stdout, write nothing to stderr, and exit with status 0.

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-001"></a>**Prints the package version**

`slcr version`, given no arguments, exits with status 0 and writes exactly `v`, the package version from `Cargo.toml`, and a newline to stdout.

<a id="REQ-003"></a>
#### 1.1.2 version usage

`slcr version` MUST take no arguments, and MUST describe itself and its options when given `--help`.

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-002"></a>**Describes itself**

`slcr version --help` exits with status 0 and prints what the subcommand does, its usage, and its options.

<a id="AC-003"></a>**Rejects an argument**

`slcr version extra` is a usage error: it exits with status 2, names the unexpected argument, and prints the usage.

<a id="REQ-004"></a>
### 1.2 init

`slcr` MUST have an `init` subcommand that creates a new specification, together with the project manifest that lists it when the working directory belongs to no project yet.

*Rationale:* Starting a specification by hand means knowing the schema's required nodes and the manifest's format before writing a single requirement. `init` writes a valid starting point instead.

All of the following must hold:

- [Creates a specification](#REQ-005)
- [Names and titles the specification](#REQ-006)
- [Starts a project](#REQ-007)
- [Joins an existing project](#REQ-008)
- [Never overwrites](#REQ-009)
- [init usage](#REQ-010)

*Terms:* [Specification](#TERM-001), [Project manifest](#TERM-003)

<a id="REQ-005"></a>
#### 1.2.1 Creates a specification

`slcr init [FILE]` MUST create the requirements file FILE, by default `SPEC.slcr.toml` in the working directory, holding a new specification whose root Section is `SEC-001` and whose empty Glossary is `SEC-002`. It MUST write the format FILE's extension names, and report `FILE: created specification NAME` on stdout.

*Terms:* [Specification](#TERM-001), [Requirements file](#TERM-002)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-004"></a>**Creates the well-known file**

`slcr init` with no FILE, in a directory outside any project, creates `SPEC.slcr.toml` holding a TOML specification with a root Section `SEC-001` and an empty Glossary `SEC-002`, and reports it.

<a id="AC-005"></a>**Writes the format the file names**

`slcr init todo-api.spec.json` writes JSON, and `slcr init todo-api.slcr.yml` writes YAML.

<a id="REQ-006"></a>
#### 1.2.2 Names and titles the specification

The new specification MUST be named `--name`, or else after FILE's name without its extension and any `.slcr` or `.spec` suffix, or, for `SPEC.slcr.*`, after the name of its directory. Its root Section MUST be titled `--title`, or else after the name. A name that is not a valid specification name (lowercase letters and digits, in dash-separated words) is an error, never silently rewritten.

*Rationale:* A name derived from a file name is a guess. Rewriting a bad guess into a valid name would give the specification a name nobody chose, which validators then have to spell.

*Terms:* [Specification](#TERM-001)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-006"></a>**Names the well-known file after its directory**

`slcr init` in a directory named `todo-api` creates a specification named `todo-api`, whose root Section is titled `todo-api`.

<a id="AC-007"></a>**Takes a name and a title**

`slcr init specs.yaml --name billing --title "Billing Service"` creates a specification named `billing` whose root Section is titled `Billing Service`.

<a id="AC-008"></a>**Never rewrites a derived name**

`slcr init "My Spec.yaml"` fails, creates nothing, and its help says that `My Spec` is not a valid name and suggests `--name`.

<a id="AC-009"></a>**Rejects an invalid name or title**

`--name "Todo API"` and `--title " padded"` are usage errors that say why the value is invalid.

<a id="REQ-007"></a>
#### 1.2.3 Starts a project

When neither the working directory nor any of its parents holds `SLCR.toml`, `slcr init` MUST also create `SLCR.toml` in the working directory, with `formatVersion` and a `specs` list holding FILE relative to it. Because `specs` holds globs, FILE MUST then be inside the working directory, contain no glob metacharacter, and not be named like the manifest.

*Terms:* [Project manifest](#TERM-003), [Project](#TERM-004)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-010"></a>**Lists the new file**

`slcr init specs/api.slcr.toml` creates `SLCR.toml` whose `specs` is `["specs/api.slcr.toml"]`.

<a id="AC-011"></a>**Rejects a file outside the working directory**

`slcr init ../SPEC.slcr.toml` outside any project fails, explains that `SLCR.toml` lists files relative to its own directory, and creates nothing.

<a id="AC-012"></a>**Rejects a path a glob would misread**

`slcr init "[draft].slcr.toml"` fails, names the characters to avoid, and creates nothing.

<a id="AC-013"></a>**Rejects a file named like the manifest**

`slcr init SLCR.toml` fails, suggests a name such as `SPEC.slcr.toml`, and creates nothing.

<a id="REQ-008"></a>
#### 1.2.4 Joins an existing project

When the working directory or a parent holds `SLCR.toml`, `slcr init` MUST leave it unchanged and say so, and MUST warn when its `specs` don't match the new file, when the new file is outside that project, or when the manifest can't be read to tell. A manifest whose name differs from `SLCR.toml` only in case MUST be an error.

*Rationale:* Editing a hand-written manifest could reorder or drop its comments, so `init` only points out what to add. Rejecting a case-only near miss keeps case-insensitive filesystems, such as macOS's, from finding a project that Linux would not.

*Terms:* [Project manifest](#TERM-003), [Project](#TERM-004)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-014"></a>**Leaves the manifest unchanged**

With `SLCR.toml` in the working directory, `slcr init` creates only the specification, reports that it left the manifest unchanged, and the manifest's bytes are unchanged.

<a id="AC-015"></a>**Finds the manifest in a parent directory**

Run in `services/billing` below a directory holding `SLCR.toml`, `slcr init` creates `services/billing/SPEC.slcr.toml` named `billing` and reports the manifest as `../../SLCR.toml`.

<a id="AC-016"></a>**Warns about a file the manifest doesn't list**

When the manifest's `specs` don't match the new file, `slcr init` succeeds with a warning whose help gives the entry to add to `specs`.

<a id="AC-017"></a>**Warns about a file outside the project**

`slcr init ../todo-api.slcr.toml` inside a project succeeds with a warning that the file is outside the project, whose `specs` can't list it.

<a id="AC-018"></a>**Warns about an unreadable manifest**

When `SLCR.toml` isn't valid TOML, `slcr init` still creates the specification, warns that it could not tell whether `specs` match it, and points at `slcr vet`.

<a id="AC-019"></a>**Rejects a misnamed manifest**

Below a directory holding `slcr.toml`, `slcr init` fails, says that the manifest's name is case-sensitive, and creates nothing.

<a id="REQ-009"></a>
#### 1.2.5 Never overwrites

`slcr init` MUST NOT overwrite an existing file, not even a dangling symlink, and MUST NOT create a missing directory. It creates the specification and the manifest together or not at all.

*Rationale:* `init` runs where files may already exist; losing one to a typo is worse than retyping the command.

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-020"></a>**Refuses an existing file**

`slcr init todo-api.yaml`, when `todo-api.yaml` exists, fails, says that it already exists, and leaves it and the directory unchanged.

<a id="AC-021"></a>**Refuses a missing directory**

`slcr init specs/todo-api.yaml`, when `specs` doesn't exist, fails with help to create the directory first, and creates nothing.

<a id="REQ-010"></a>
#### 1.2.6 init usage

`slcr init` MUST take at most one FILE, MUST reject a FILE whose extension names no supported format, and MUST describe itself, its arguments, and its options when given `--help`.

*Terms:* [Requirements file](#TERM-002)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-022"></a>**Describes itself**

`slcr init --help` describes FILE and its default, `--name`, and `--title`.

<a id="AC-023"></a>**Takes at most one file**

`slcr init a.yaml b.yaml` is a usage error naming `b.yaml`.

<a id="AC-024"></a>**Rejects an unsupported format**

`slcr init SPEC.md` fails, lists the supported extensions, and creates nothing.

<a id="REQ-011"></a>
### 1.3 vet

`slcr` MUST have a `vet` subcommand that checks requirements files, or a whole project, against every rule of the SLCR formats, including the invariants their schemas can't express, and reports every finding at once. It runs nothing and never uses the network.

*Rationale:* Like `terraform validate`, vetting is fast, offline, and deterministic, so it can run on every save and in every sandbox, and it finds a broken specification before `check` spends time running validators against it.

All of the following must hold:

- [Vets requirements files](#REQ-012)
- [Warnings pass unless denied](#REQ-013)
- [Reports in JSON](#REQ-014)
- [Vets the project](#REQ-015)
- [Discovers specifications](#REQ-016)
- [Vets validator files](#REQ-017)
- [Vets pinned descriptors](#REQ-018)
- [vet usage](#REQ-019)

*Terms:* [Finding](#TERM-005)

<a id="REQ-012"></a>
#### 1.3.1 Vets requirements files

`slcr vet FILE...` MUST load each FILE and write its status to stdout (`ok`, its counts of violations and warnings, or `could not be loaded`) and each of its findings to stderr, labeled in the file's source where the problem has a location. A file that can't be read, can't be parsed, or names no supported format MUST be reported without stopping the others. `slcr vet` fails when any file could not be loaded or breaks an invariant.

*Terms:* [Requirements file](#TERM-002), [Finding](#TERM-005)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-025"></a>**Passes the canon example in every format**

`slcr vet` given the canon `todo-api` example as YAML, JSON, and TOML reports each file `ok` and exits with status 0.

<a id="AC-026"></a>**Reports every finding in every file**

Given a valid file, one with a warning, one with a violation, one that isn't valid YAML, one with an invalid ID, a missing file, and a Markdown file, `slcr vet` reports a status for each of the seven, labels the invalid ID at its line, says that vetting failed for 5 of 7 files, and exits with status 1.

<a id="REQ-013"></a>
#### 1.3.2 Warnings pass unless denied

A warning MUST be reported without failing `slcr vet`, unless `--deny-warnings` is given, which makes any warning fail its file and the command.

*Rationale:* Warnings flag what is probably a mistake, such as a body that never states its modality. Teams that want a clean specification can enforce one in CI without forcing it on every draft.

*Terms:* [Finding](#TERM-005)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-027"></a>**Fails on a warning only when warnings are denied**

A file whose only finding is a warning passes `slcr vet` with the warning on stderr, and fails `slcr vet --deny-warnings` with help naming the flag.

<a id="REQ-014"></a>
#### 1.3.3 Reports in JSON

`slcr vet --format json` MUST write one JSON document to stdout instead of human output: whether vetting passed and, for each file, its path, whether it passed, its counts, and its findings, each with a kebab-case `code`, its fields, its severity, its message, and any help. A file that could not be loaded carries its error instead. In project mode, the document MUST also hold a `project` object for the manifest's problems and a `validators` array for the validator files. `--format human` is the default.

*Rationale:* Agents and editors consume findings programmatically; a stable `code` lets them act on a kind of finding without parsing its prose.

*Terms:* [Finding](#TERM-005)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-028"></a>**Reports files in JSON**

`slcr vet --format json` given the seven files of AC-026 writes one document whose files carry their findings or errors, and exits with status 1.

<a id="AC-029"></a>**Reports denied warnings in JSON**

With `--deny-warnings`, a file whose only finding is a warning does not pass in the JSON document.

<a id="AC-030"></a>**Reports the project in JSON**

In project mode, the document holds the manifest's problems in `project`, including a manifest that can't be parsed, alongside the files.

<a id="AC-031"></a>**Reports validator and descriptor problems in JSON**

Validator files' problems appear in `validators`, and pinned descriptors' problems in `project`, each with its own `code`.

<a id="AC-032"></a>**Writes human output by default**

`slcr vet --format human` writes the human report: status lines on stdout and diagnostics on stderr.

<a id="REQ-015"></a>
#### 1.3.4 Vets the project

Given no FILE, `slcr vet` MUST vet the project: it finds `SLCR.toml` in the working directory or a parent, vets every requirements file the manifest's `specs` match, and reports the manifest as one more file with its own status. It names every file relative to the working directory. Outside a project, it MUST fail with help on creating a manifest, and a manifest whose name differs from `SLCR.toml` only in case MUST be an error.

*Terms:* [Project manifest](#TERM-003), [Project](#TERM-004)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-033"></a>**Vets the project**

In a project whose `specs` match three specifications, `slcr vet` reports `SLCR.toml: ok` and each specification `ok`, and exits with status 0.

<a id="AC-034"></a>**Names files from the working directory**

Run in `docs/api`, `slcr vet` names the manifest `../../SLCR.toml` and the files beside it by their bare names.

<a id="AC-035"></a>**Reports every finding in the project**

In a project holding a valid specification, one with a warning, one with a violation, and one that can't be parsed, `slcr vet --deny-warnings` reports all of them and fails.

<a id="AC-036"></a>**Requires a project**

`slcr vet` with no FILE outside any project fails, and its help shows a minimal manifest.

<a id="AC-037"></a>**Rejects a misnamed manifest**

`slcr vet` beside `slcr.toml` fails, saying that the manifest's name is case-sensitive.

<a id="REQ-016"></a>
#### 1.3.5 Discovers specifications

`slcr vet` MUST expand each `specs` pattern as a glob relative to the project root, in which `*` and `?` never cross a `/` and `**` does, seeing hidden files but skipping `.git` and whatever git ignores. A pattern that is invalid or matches nothing, a match that is a validator file or has no supported format's extension, and two files whose specifications share a name MUST each be a problem of the manifest, as MUST a manifest that breaks its schema, such as a pattern that leaves the project.

*Rationale:* A pattern that silently matches nothing would leave a specification unvetted and unchecked while every command passes.

*Terms:* [Project manifest](#TERM-003), [Project](#TERM-004)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-038"></a>**Searches hidden directories and skips ignored files**

`docs/**/*.slcr.{json,toml}` matches a specification under `docs/.drafts` but not an unparsable one under a directory that `.gitignore` lists.

<a id="AC-039"></a>**Reports a pattern that matches nothing**

A `specs` pattern that matches no file is a manifest problem whose help mentions typos and `.gitignore`.

<a id="AC-040"></a>**Reports an invalid pattern**

The pattern `specs/[a` is a manifest problem that explains the glob syntax.

<a id="AC-041"></a>**Reports a pattern that matches a validator file**

A pattern matching `.validators.slcr.toml` is a manifest problem whose help shows how to narrow it.

<a id="AC-042"></a>**Reports a match of no supported format**

A pattern matching `notes.md` is a manifest problem that lists the supported extensions.

<a id="AC-043"></a>**Reports duplicate specification names**

Two files that both name their specification `todo-api` are one manifest problem naming both files.

<a id="AC-044"></a>**Rejects a pattern that leaves the project**

A manifest whose `specs` holds `../SPEC.slcr.yml` can't be loaded, and the error labels the pattern in `SLCR.toml`.

<a id="REQ-017"></a>
#### 1.3.6 Vets validator files

In project mode, `slcr vet` MUST find every validator file in the project, however `specs` reads, by the same walk that finds specifications, and report each with a status line. Each problem MUST be labeled at its validator in the file's source: a requirement that doesn't resolve to a specification and a requirement in it, an acceptance criterion that isn't the requirement's own, a tool the manifest doesn't declare, a `with` that the tool's validator schema rejects (one problem per schema error), and a validator identical to an earlier one. Two validator files in one directory MUST be a problem of the manifest.

*Terms:* [Validator](#TERM-006), [Validator file](#TERM-007)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-045"></a>**Vets validator files in every format**

Validator files in TOML, JSON, and YAML are each reported `ok`, and one in a directory that `.gitignore` lists is skipped.

<a id="AC-046"></a>**Names validator files from the working directory**

Run in `src/views`, `slcr vet` names validator files relative to it.

<a id="AC-047"></a>**Labels every problem at its validator**

A validator file with an unknown specification, an unknown requirement, another requirement's criterion, an undeclared tool, a `with` that breaks the schema twice, and a repeated validator reports 7 problems, each labeled in the file, with help listing what does exist.

<a id="AC-048"></a>**Labels problems in JSON and YAML**

Problems in validator files written in JSON and in YAML are labeled at their location too.

<a id="AC-049"></a>**Reports a validator file that breaks its schema**

A validator file whose `criterion` is `AC-1` can't be loaded, and the error labels the value.

<a id="AC-050"></a>**Reports two validator files in one directory**

`.validators.slcr.toml` and `.validators.slcr.yml` in one directory are a manifest problem, and both files are still vetted.

<a id="REQ-018"></a>
#### 1.3.7 Vets pinned descriptors

For each tool the manifest declares, `slcr vet` MUST report a problem of the manifest when the descriptor store doesn't hold the descriptor the tool pins, holds bytes that don't hash to the pin, holds an invalid descriptor, or holds one whose version isn't the declared one, with help naming `slcr tools install` or `slcr tools update`, whichever fixes it. It MUST only read the store, never fetching or installing a descriptor.

*Rationale:* Without its descriptor, `with` can't be checked against the tool's schema and the tool can't run; reporting that offline tells the user exactly which command restores it.

*Terms:* [Tool descriptor](#TERM-008), [Descriptor store](#TERM-009), [Pin](#TERM-010)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-051"></a>**Reports a descriptor that is not installed**

When the store lacks a pinned descriptor, `slcr vet` reports it with help naming `slcr tools install`, skips checking `with` against its schema, and installs nothing.

<a id="AC-052"></a>**Reports a corrupted descriptor**

When the store's copy no longer hashes to its pin, `slcr vet` says so, with help naming `slcr tools install`.

<a id="AC-053"></a>**Reports an invalid descriptor**

When the pinned descriptor's argv names a `with` field its schema lacks, `slcr vet` reports why it is invalid, with help naming `slcr tools update`.

<a id="AC-054"></a>**Reports an undeclared version**

When the manifest declares version 0.9.0 but the pinned descriptor is 1.0.0, `slcr vet` reports both versions, with help naming `slcr tools update`.

<a id="REQ-019"></a>
#### 1.3.8 vet usage

`slcr vet` MUST take any number of FILEs, MUST reject a `--format` other than `human` or `json`, and MUST describe itself, its arguments, and its options when given `--help`.

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-055"></a>**Describes itself**

`slcr vet --help` describes FILE, project mode, `--deny-warnings`, and `--format`.

<a id="AC-056"></a>**Rejects an unknown format**

`slcr vet --format xml` is a usage error listing `human` and `json`.

<a id="REQ-020"></a>
### 1.4 render

`slcr` MUST have a `render` subcommand that renders a specification as canonical Markdown, so that people can read it, and review changes to it, wherever they read code.

*Rationale:* A rendering committed beside its specification shows up readably on GitHub and in code review, where the YAML, JSON, or TOML of a large graph does not.

All of the following must hold:

- [Renders canonical Markdown](#REQ-021)
- [Chooses its output](#REQ-022)
- [Replaces only its own output](#REQ-023)
- [Reports findings](#REQ-024)
- [Expects no diff](#REQ-025)
- [render usage](#REQ-026)

*Terms:* [Rendering](#TERM-011)

<a id="REQ-021"></a>
#### 1.4.1 Renders canonical Markdown

`slcr render [FILE]` MUST render the specification in FILE, by default `SPEC.slcr.toml`, as canonical Markdown, the same specification always rendering to the same bytes. By default it MUST write it beside FILE, named after FILE without its extension and any `.slcr` or `.spec` suffix, plus `.md`, and report `OUTPUT: rendered NAME`.

*Terms:* [Requirements file](#TERM-002), [Rendering](#TERM-011)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-057"></a>**Renders the canon example beside the well-known file**

`slcr render` beside the canon `todo-api` example in `SPEC.slcr.toml` writes `SPEC.md` holding exactly the golden rendering `tests/fixtures/todo-api.md`, and nothing else.

<a id="AC-058"></a>**Names the Markdown after the file**

`slcr render specs/todo-api.spec.yaml` writes `specs/todo-api.md`.

<a id="AC-059"></a>**Needs an output for a file named only by its suffix**

`slcr render .spec.yaml` fails, since no name is left for the Markdown, and its help suggests `--output`.

<a id="REQ-022"></a>
#### 1.4.2 Chooses its output

`slcr render --output PATH` (or `-o PATH`) MUST write the Markdown to PATH instead, and `-o -` to stdout. It MUST NOT create a missing directory, and MUST NOT write over the requirements file being rendered, even with `--force`.

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-060"></a>**Writes to the output**

`slcr render --output docs/API.md` writes the rendering to `docs/API.md` and nowhere else.

<a id="AC-061"></a>**Writes to stdout**

`slcr render -o -` writes the rendering to stdout and creates no file.

<a id="AC-062"></a>**Refuses a missing directory**

`slcr render -o docs/SPEC.md`, when `docs` doesn't exist, fails with help to create it first, and creates nothing.

<a id="AC-063"></a>**Never writes over the requirements file**

`slcr render --output ./SPEC.slcr.toml --force` fails, saying that this is the file being rendered, and leaves it unchanged.

<a id="REQ-023"></a>
#### 1.4.3 Replaces only its own output

`slcr render` MUST replace an existing output only when it starts with the comment that marks a file `slcr` generated, unless `--force` is given, and MUST replace it atomically. An output that already holds the rendering MUST be left untouched and reported `up to date`.

*Rationale:* A hand-written `SPEC.md` is someone's work. Leaving an up-to-date file untouched keeps its modification time, so build tools don't rebuild what didn't change.

*Terms:* [Rendering](#TERM-011)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-064"></a>**Replaces its own earlier output**

`slcr render` replaces a stale `SPEC.md` that starts with the generated-file comment with the current rendering.

<a id="AC-065"></a>**Replaces a hand-written file only by force**

`slcr render` refuses to replace a hand-written `SPEC.md`, suggesting `--force` or `--output` and leaving it unchanged; `slcr render --force` replaces it.

<a id="AC-066"></a>**Leaves an up-to-date output alone**

`slcr render` reports `SPEC.md: up to date` when `SPEC.md` already holds the rendering.

<a id="REQ-024"></a>
#### 1.4.4 Reports findings

`slcr render` MUST write the specification's findings to stderr as `slcr vet` reports them, render a specification whose findings are only warnings, and refuse one that breaks an invariant, writing nothing.

*Depends on:* [Vets requirements files](#REQ-012)

*Terms:* [Finding](#TERM-005)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-067"></a>**Renders despite warnings**

A specification with a warning renders, with the warning on stderr.

<a id="AC-068"></a>**Refuses a broken specification**

A specification with a violation fails to render, with the violation on stderr and help to fix it, and no Markdown is written.

<a id="REQ-025"></a>
#### 1.4.5 Expects no diff

`slcr render --expect-no-diff` MUST write nothing, and fail unless the output already holds exactly what FILE renders to, saying whether the output is missing or the first line on which it differs. It compares a file, so it MUST refuse stdout as the output, and it conflicts with `--force`.

*Rationale:* CI and pre-commit hooks use it to keep a committed rendering in step with its specification, as this repository does with `SPEC.md`. The flag avoids the word "check", which means running validators.

*Terms:* [Rendering](#TERM-011)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-069"></a>**Passes an up-to-date output**

`slcr render --expect-no-diff` reports `SPEC.md: up to date` and exits with status 0 when it is.

<a id="AC-070"></a>**Compares the chosen output**

`slcr render --expect-no-diff --output docs/API.md` compares `docs/API.md`.

<a id="AC-071"></a>**Fails on a missing output**

`slcr render --expect-no-diff` without `SPEC.md` fails, saying it does not exist, and creates nothing.

<a id="AC-072"></a>**Fails on a stale output**

`slcr render --expect-no-diff` with a stale `SPEC.md` fails, naming the first line that differs, and leaves the file unchanged.

<a id="AC-073"></a>**Cannot compare stdout**

`slcr render --expect-no-diff -o -` fails, with help to name a file instead.

<a id="AC-074"></a>**Conflicts with force**

`slcr render --expect-no-diff --force` is a usage error.

<a id="REQ-026"></a>
#### 1.4.6 render usage

`slcr render` MUST take at most one FILE, MUST fail on a FILE that can't be read or names no supported format, and MUST describe itself, its arguments, and its options when given `--help`.

*Terms:* [Requirements file](#TERM-002)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-075"></a>**Describes itself**

`slcr render --help` describes FILE and its default, `--output`, `--force`, and `--expect-no-diff`.

<a id="AC-076"></a>**Takes at most one file**

`slcr render a.yaml b.yaml` is a usage error naming `b.yaml`.

<a id="AC-077"></a>**Rejects an unsupported format**

`slcr render SPEC.md` fails, listing the supported extensions.

<a id="AC-078"></a>**Reports a missing file**

`slcr render` without `SPEC.slcr.toml` fails, saying it could not read it.

<a id="REQ-027"></a>
### 1.5 query

`slcr` MUST have a `query` subcommand that runs a read-only query, in the SLCR query profile of GQL, against the graph of a specification, and writes the rows it returns.

*Rationale:* Agents and people ask structural questions of a specification, such as what transitively refines a requirement or which MUST requirements lack acceptance criteria. A query answers them from the graph without anyone parsing YAML, JSON, or TOML by hand.

All of the following must hold:

- [Runs queries](#REQ-028)
- [Binds parameters](#REQ-029)
- [Writes rows in a chosen format](#REQ-030)
- [Explains a query that can't run](#REQ-031)
- [Queries only a sound specification](#REQ-032)
- [query usage](#REQ-033)

*Terms:* [SLCR query profile](#TERM-012)

<a id="REQ-028"></a>
#### 1.5.1 Runs queries

`slcr query QUERY [FILE]` MUST run QUERY against the graph of the specification in FILE, by default `SPEC.slcr.toml`, whatever its format, and write the rows to stdout. A node MUST be written as its SLCR ID wherever it appears, inside lists too, and an edge as `(SOURCE)-[:LABEL]->(TARGET)`.

*Terms:* [Specification](#TERM-001), [SLCR query profile](#TERM-012)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-079"></a>**Reads the well-known file**

Against the canon example in `SPEC.slcr.toml`, a query for what transitively refines REQ-001 writes REQ-002, REQ-003, and REQ-004 with their modalities, and `(3 rows)`.

<a id="AC-080"></a>**Reads every format alike**

The same query against the canon example in YAML, JSON, and TOML succeeds with identical output.

<a id="AC-081"></a>**Names nodes and edges by ID**

Returning a requirement, its `REFINES` edges, and their targets writes `REQ-004`, `(REQ-004)-[:REFINES]->(REQ-002)`, and `REQ-002`.

<a id="AC-082"></a>**Names nodes in lists by ID**

`collect_list` of each Section's children writes lists of IDs, such as `[SEC-002, SEC-003, SEC-004, SEC-005, SEC-006]`.

<a id="AC-083"></a>**Reports no rows**

A query that matches nothing writes its header and `(0 rows)`, and succeeds.

<a id="REQ-029"></a>
#### 1.5.2 Binds parameters

`slcr query --param NAME=JSON` (or `-p NAME=JSON`) MUST bind the parameter `$NAME` to the JSON value, once per name. A value that isn't JSON, an argument without `=`, and a name written with its `$` MUST be usage errors, and binding a name twice MUST be an error.

*Rationale:* Parameters keep values out of the query text, so a script never has to quote an ID into GQL.

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-084"></a>**Binds parameters**

`--param modality='"MAY"'` and `-p 'ids=["REQ-009", "REQ-010", "REQ-099"]'` bind a string and a list, and the query writes REQ-009 and REQ-010.

<a id="AC-085"></a>**Rejects a parameter bound twice**

`-p n=1 -p n=2` fails, saying that `$n` is bound more than once.

<a id="AC-086"></a>**Rejects a value that is not JSON**

`--param id=REQ-001` is a usage error whose message shows how to quote a JSON string.

<a id="AC-087"></a>**Rejects a parameter without a value**

`--param id` is a usage error expecting `NAME=JSON`.

<a id="AC-088"></a>**Rejects a name written with its dollar**

`--param '$id=1'` is a usage error saying to drop the `$`.

<a id="REQ-030"></a>
#### 1.5.3 Writes rows in a chosen format

`slcr query` MUST write rows as an aligned table, with a header, a rule, and a row count, by default or under `--format table`; as tab-separated values with a header line under `--format tsv`; and as one JSON document of `columns` and `rows` under `--format json`, in which an edge is an object of its `label`, `source`, and `target`. Any other format MUST be a usage error.

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-089"></a>**Writes a table**

`--format table` writes the aligned table with `(1 row)`.

<a id="AC-090"></a>**Writes TSV**

`--format tsv` writes a header line and one tab-separated line per row, a null as an empty field.

<a id="AC-091"></a>**Writes JSON**

`--format json` writes `columns` and `rows`, an edge as an object of `label`, `source`, and `target`, and numbers, nulls, booleans, and lists as JSON.

<a id="AC-092"></a>**Rejects an unknown format**

`--format csv` is a usage error listing `table`, `tsv`, and `json`.

<a id="REQ-031"></a>
#### 1.5.4 Explains a query that can't run

A query that can't run MUST fail with an explanation: a syntax error, or a feature outside the profile, labeled where it is in the query, the latter with help linking the profile; an undefined variable or a missing parameter as an invalid query; and an error raised while running, such as arithmetic on a string, as a failed query. The query MUST be parsed before FILE is read.

*Rationale:* Parsing first reports a typo in the query immediately, even when the file is large or missing.

*Terms:* [SLCR query profile](#TERM-012)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-093"></a>**Labels a syntax error**

`MATCH (r:Requirement RETURN r` fails as not valid GQL, labeling `RETURN` with what was expected.

<a id="AC-094"></a>**Parses before reading the file**

A query with a syntax error, given a FILE that doesn't exist, reports the syntax error, not the missing file.

<a id="AC-095"></a>**Labels a feature outside the profile**

`OPTIONAL MATCH` fails, labeling `OPTIONAL` as outside the profile, with help linking `PROFILE.md`.

<a id="AC-096"></a>**Reports an undefined variable**

`MATCH (r) RETURN s` fails as invalid, naming the undefined variable `s`.

<a id="AC-097"></a>**Reports a missing parameter**

A query using `$id` with no `--param id=...` fails as invalid, naming `$id`.

<a id="AC-098"></a>**Reports a query that fails while running**

`MATCH (r) RETURN r.id + 1` fails, explaining the arithmetic on a string and an integer.

<a id="REQ-032"></a>
#### 1.5.5 Queries only a sound specification

`slcr query` MUST write the specification's findings to stderr as `slcr vet` reports them, query a specification whose findings are only warnings, and refuse one that breaks an invariant.

*Depends on:* [Vets requirements files](#REQ-012)

*Terms:* [Finding](#TERM-005)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-099"></a>**Queries despite warnings**

A specification with a warning is queried, with the warning on stderr.

<a id="AC-100"></a>**Refuses a broken specification**

A specification with a violation is not queried: the violation is on stderr, with help to fix it.

<a id="REQ-033"></a>
#### 1.5.6 query usage

`slcr query` MUST require a QUERY, take at most one FILE, fail on a FILE that can't be read or names no supported format, and describe itself, its arguments, and its options when given `--help`.

*Terms:* [Requirements file](#TERM-002)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-101"></a>**Describes itself**

`slcr query --help` describes QUERY, FILE and its default, `--param`, and `--format`.

<a id="AC-102"></a>**Requires a query**

`slcr query` alone is a usage error naming `<QUERY>`.

<a id="AC-103"></a>**Takes at most one file**

`slcr query "RETURN 1" a.yaml b.yaml` is a usage error naming `b.yaml`.

<a id="AC-104"></a>**Reports a missing file**

`slcr query "RETURN 1"` without `SPEC.slcr.toml` fails, saying it could not read it.

<a id="AC-105"></a>**Rejects an unsupported format**

`slcr query "RETURN 1" SPEC.md` fails, listing the supported extensions.

<a id="REQ-034"></a>
### 1.6 slice

`slcr` MUST have a `slice` subcommand that writes the slice of one requirement: everything in the specification needed to understand and implement it, and nothing more, as Markdown.

*Rationale:* An agent implementing one requirement works best with a bounded, self-contained context. The slice gives it exactly that, instead of the whole document or a hand-picked excerpt that misses a dependency.

All of the following must hold:

- [Writes the slice](#REQ-035)
- [Slices only a sound specification](#REQ-036)
- [Names one requirement](#REQ-037)
- [slice usage](#REQ-038)

*Terms:* [Slice](#TERM-013)

<a id="REQ-035"></a>
#### 1.6.1 Writes the slice

`slcr slice REQUIREMENT [FILE]` MUST write the slice of REQUIREMENT in the specification in FILE, by default `SPEC.slcr.toml`, whatever its format, to stdout as Markdown, and write no file. The slice MUST hold the requirement's ancestors as headings with their bodies; the requirement and the requirements that refine it, in full; what it refines, and the `dependsOn` closure of it and its refinements, under "Related requirements", each with a breadcrumb of its ancestors; and a Glossary of the terms all of these use. Nodes keep their document numbers, and a reference to a node the slice leaves out is its plain title, so every link resolves within the slice.

*Terms:* [Rendering](#TERM-011), [Slice](#TERM-013)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-106"></a>**Slices from the well-known file**

`slcr slice REQ-005` beside the canon example in `SPEC.slcr.toml` writes the controller's slice to stdout and creates no file.

<a id="AC-107"></a>**Matches the golden slice in every format**

The canon example in YAML, JSON, and TOML each slices REQ-005 to exactly the golden file `tests/fixtures/todo-api.REQ-005.md`, with nothing on stderr.

<a id="AC-108"></a>**Brings a shared requirement's other parent**

REQ-004, which is housed under REQ-002 and also refines REQ-003, slices to a document holding its ancestors and, under "Related requirements", REQ-003 with its breadcrumb.

<a id="AC-109"></a>**Brings refinements housed elsewhere**

The slice of REQ-003 holds REQ-004, which refines it though it is housed under REQ-002.

<a id="REQ-036"></a>
#### 1.6.2 Slices only a sound specification

`slcr slice` MUST write the specification's findings to stderr as `slcr vet` reports them, slice a specification whose findings are only warnings, and refuse one that breaks an invariant.

*Depends on:* [Vets requirements files](#REQ-012)

*Terms:* [Finding](#TERM-005)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-110"></a>**Slices despite warnings**

A specification with a warning is sliced, with the warning on stderr.

<a id="AC-111"></a>**Refuses a broken specification**

A specification with a violation is not sliced: the violation is on stderr, with help to fix it.

<a id="REQ-037"></a>
#### 1.6.3 Names one requirement

REQUIREMENT MUST be a requirement ID spelled canonically, such as `REQ-005`; anything else, including the ID of a Section or another kind of node, MUST be a usage error. An ID that the specification lacks MUST fail, with help showing how to list its requirements.

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-112"></a>**Reports a requirement the specification lacks**

`slcr slice REQ-099` fails, saying that `SPEC.slcr.toml` has no REQ-099, with help giving a `slcr query` that lists the requirements.

<a id="AC-113"></a>**Rejects an invalid requirement ID**

`slcr slice REQ-5` is a usage error saying that it is not a valid requirement ID.

<a id="AC-114"></a>**Rejects an ID of another kind**

`slcr slice SEC-001` is a usage error saying that it is not a valid requirement ID.

<a id="REQ-038"></a>
#### 1.6.4 slice usage

`slcr slice` MUST require a REQUIREMENT, take at most one FILE, fail on a FILE that can't be read or names no supported format, and describe itself, its arguments, and its options when given `--help`.

*Terms:* [Requirements file](#TERM-002)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-115"></a>**Describes itself**

`slcr slice --help` describes REQUIREMENT, and FILE and its default.

<a id="AC-116"></a>**Requires a requirement**

`slcr slice` alone is a usage error naming `<REQUIREMENT>`.

<a id="AC-117"></a>**Takes at most one file**

`slcr slice REQ-001 a.yaml b.yaml` is a usage error naming `b.yaml`.

<a id="AC-118"></a>**Reports a missing file**

`slcr slice REQ-001` without `SPEC.slcr.toml` fails, saying it could not read it.

<a id="AC-119"></a>**Rejects an unsupported format**

`slcr slice REQ-001 SPEC.md` fails, listing the supported extensions.

<a id="REQ-039"></a>
### 1.7 tools

`slcr` MUST have a `tools` subcommand that manages the tools a project's validators run, through its manifest: declaring, updating, installing, removing, listing, and showing them.

*Rationale:* A validator names a tool, not a command line. Declaring each tool once in the manifest, pinned to the exact descriptor that says how to run it, keeps every validator file short, and makes the commands that run on a machine reviewable in the manifest's history.

All of the following must hold:

- [Works on the project's manifest](#REQ-040)
- [Names tools](#REQ-041)

*Terms:* [Project manifest](#TERM-003), [Tool](#TERM-014)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-120"></a>**Lists its subcommands**

`slcr tools --help` describes `add`, `update`, `install`, `remove`, `list`, and `show`.

<a id="REQ-040"></a>
#### 1.7.1 Works on the project's manifest

Every `slcr tools` subcommand MUST find the project as `slcr vet` does, by walking up from the working directory to the nearest `SLCR.toml`, and name the manifest relative to the working directory. Outside a project it MUST fail with help on creating a manifest. A manifest whose name differs from `SLCR.toml` only in case, and one that breaks the manifest schema, MUST be errors that change nothing.

*Depends on:* [Vets the project](#REQ-015)

*Terms:* [Project manifest](#TERM-003), [Project](#TERM-004)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-121"></a>**Finds the project above the working directory**

Run in `crates/api`, `slcr tools add`, `update`, `remove`, and `install` work on the manifest two directories up, which they name `../../SLCR.toml`.

<a id="AC-122"></a>**Requires a manifest**

Outside any project, every `slcr tools` subcommand fails, with help showing a minimal manifest, and creates nothing.

<a id="AC-123"></a>**Rejects a misnamed manifest**

Beside `slcr.toml`, `slcr tools add`, `update`, and `remove` fail, saying that the manifest's name is case-sensitive.

<a id="AC-124"></a>**Refuses an invalid manifest**

When `SLCR.toml` breaks its schema, such as with a `specs` pattern or a `path` source that leaves the project, `slcr tools add`, `update`, and `remove` fail, labeling the problem, and leave it unchanged.

<a id="REQ-041"></a>
#### 1.7.2 Names tools

A tool's name, the key of its entry in the manifest's `tools`, by which validators refer to it, MUST be lowercase letters and digits in dash-separated words, such as `cargo-insta`. Any other name given to a `slcr tools` subcommand MUST be a usage error.

*Terms:* [Tool](#TERM-014)

*Acceptance criteria:*

<a id="AC-125"></a>**Rejects an invalid name**

`Nextest`, given to `slcr tools add --as`, `update`, `remove`, or `show`, is a usage error saying that it is not a valid tool name.

<a id="SEC-002"></a>
## 2. Glossary

<dl>
<dt><a id="TERM-009"></a>Descriptor store</dt>
<dd>

A content-addressed store of tool descriptors in `slcr`'s data directory, filed by pin and shared by every project on the machine. Only `slcr tools add`, `update`, and `install`, and `slcr check`, ever fill it.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-005"></a>Finding</dt>
<dd>

Something vetting reports about a specification. A violation breaks an invariant of the format, such as a dangling reference or a `refines` cycle, and fails vetting; a warning, such as a body that never states its modality, fails it only when warnings are denied.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-010"></a>Pin</dt>
<dd>

`blake3:` followed by the 64 lowercase hex digits of a descriptor's BLAKE3 hash. The manifest records each tool's pin, so a validator always runs exactly the descriptor that was declared, wherever it came from.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-004"></a>Project</dt>
<dd>

The directory tree under a project manifest. A command that works on a project finds it by walking up from the working directory to the nearest `SLCR.toml`, and names files relative to the working directory.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-003"></a>Project manifest</dt>
<dd>

*Also called:* SLCR.toml

The file `SLCR.toml`, whose directory is a project's root. Its `specs` list the project's requirements files as globs relative to that directory, and its `tools` declare and pin the tools that the project's validators run.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-011"></a>Rendering</dt>
<dd>

The canonical Markdown of a specification: a comment saying that `slcr` generated it, then every Section and Requirement as a numbered heading, in document order, with its body, rationale, refinements, dependencies, terms, and acceptance criteria, and finally the Glossary. Every node is preceded by a hidden anchor named by its ID, and every cross-reference is a link to one, so IDs never appear in the visible text.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-002"></a>Requirements file</dt>
<dd>

A file that holds one specification, in the format its extension names: YAML (`.yaml` or `.yml`), JSON (`.json`), or TOML (`.toml`). The well-known one, which commands read when given no FILE, is `SPEC.slcr.toml`.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-012"></a>SLCR query profile</dt>
<dd>

The read-only subset of GQL that `slcr query` runs, and the property graph a specification maps to: nodes labeled `Section`, `Requirement`, `AcceptanceCriterion`, and `Term`, carrying their fields as properties, and edges `CONTAINS` and `HAS_CRITERION` (each with a `position`), `REFINES`, `DEPENDS_ON`, and `USES_TERM`. `PROFILE.md` in `wack/gql-rust` specifies it.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-013"></a>Slice</dt>
<dd>

The part of a specification that one requirement needs, rendered like the whole document: the requirement's ancestors (bodies only), the requirement and its refinement descendants in full, what it refines, the requirements it and its descendants depend on, and the terms all of them use. A node included for several reasons is shown in the most detail any of them calls for.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-001"></a>Specification</dt>
<dd>

An SLCR requirements document: a named tree of Sections and Requirements, the acceptance criteria of those Requirements, the cross edges between them (`refines`, `dependsOn`, and `usesTerm`), and a Glossary of Terms. Its name, such as `todo-api`, qualifies its requirements' IDs elsewhere, as in `todo-api/REQ-002`.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-014"></a>Tool</dt>
<dd>

An external program that validators run, such as `cargo insta`. A project declares it in its manifest's `tools`, under a name, with the version and the source (`{ path }` in the project, or `{ url }` over HTTPS) of its descriptor, and that descriptor's pin.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-008"></a>Tool descriptor</dt>
<dd>

*Also called:* Descriptor

A declarative TOML file that tells SLCR how to run one tool: its argument vector, whose placeholders are filled from a validator's `with`; its working directory and environment; the JSON Schema that every validator's `with` must satisfy; and which exit codes pass. A descriptor is never executed itself, and is never run through a shell.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-006"></a>Validator</dt>
<dd>

One entry of a validator file: a qualified requirement, such as `slcr/REQ-002`, optionally one of its acceptance criteria, the tool that checks it, and the fields (`with`) the tool's validator schema requires. A validator is green when its tool exits with a passing code, and red otherwise.

</dd>
<dt><a id="TERM-007"></a>Validator file</dt>
<dd>

A file named `.validators.slcr.toml`, `.validators.slcr.json`, `.validators.slcr.yaml`, or `.validators.slcr.yml`, holding a list of validators. A directory holds at most one, and commands find every one in the project, so validators can sit beside the code they check.

</dd>
</dl>
